description: KNaTi₂(PO₅)₂ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pna2₁ space group. K is bonded in a 9-coordinate geometry to nine O atoms. There are a spread of K-O bond distances ranging from 2.74-3.17 Å. Na is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.56-2.98 Å. There are two inequivalent Ti sites. In the first Ti site, Ti is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted TiO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent TiO₆ octahedra and corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 44-48°. There are a spread of Ti-O bond distances ranging from 1.77-2.18 Å. In the second Ti site, Ti is bonded to six O atoms to form TiO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent TiO₆ octahedra and corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 44-48°. There are a spread of Ti-O bond distances ranging from 1.80-2.08 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four TiO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 45-50°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.54-1.56 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four TiO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 44-52°. There is one shorter (1.53 Å) and three longer (1.56 Å) P-O bond lengths. There are ten inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one K, one Na, and two Ti atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one K, one Ti, and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one K, one Na, one Ti, and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one K, one Na, one Ti, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 150 degrees geometry to one Ti and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one K, one Na, one Ti, and one P atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one K, one Na, one Ti, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one K, one Na, and two Ti atoms. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one K, one Na, one Ti, and one P atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one K, one Na, one Ti, and one P atom.
